alpha.definition: A position where the two hands are at opposite grid points (180 degrees apart).
examples: alpha1: hands at N and S
alpha3: hands at E and W

beta.definition: A position where both hands are at the same grid point (0 degrees apart).
examples: beta1: both hands at N
beta5: both hands at NE

gamma.definition: A position where the hands form a right angle (90 degrees apart on adjacent grid points).
examples: gamma1: hands at N and E
gamma5: hands at N and NW

zeta.definition: A position where the hands form an obtuse angle (greater than 90 degrees). Introduced in Level 4 with skewed grid mode.
examples: One hand cardinal, one intercardinal, forming ~135 degree angle

eta.definition: A position where the hands form an acute angle (less than 90 degrees). Introduced in Level 4 with skewed grid mode.
examples: One hand cardinal, one intercardinal, forming ~45 degree angle

pro.definition: A rotation direction where the prop spins WITH the direction of hand travel. Also called 'prospin'.
examples: If hand moves clockwise, prop rotates clockwise
Like a wheel rolling forward

anti.definition: A rotation direction where the prop spins AGAINST the direction of hand travel. Also called 'antispin'.
examples: If hand moves clockwise, prop rotates counter-clockwise
Creates 'petal' patterns

static.definition: A motion type where the hand stays at its current grid point (no movement). The prop may still rotate.
examples: Type 6 letters (alpha, beta, gamma) have both hands static
Type 2 letters have one static hand

shift.definition: A motion type where the hand moves to an adjacent grid point (90 degree movement).
examples: N to E is a shift
NE to N is a shift
Type 1 and Type 2 letters use shift

dash.definition: A motion type where the hand moves to the opposite grid point (180 degree movement).
examples: N to S is a dash
NE to SW is a dash
Type 4 and Type 5 letters use dash

dual-shift.definition: A letter type (Type 1) where both hands shift simultaneously to adjacent points.
examples: Letters A through V
Most common letter type with 22 letters

cross-shift.definition: A letter type (Type 3) where one hand shifts and one hand dashes. Also called 'dash letters' due to the '-' suffix.
examples: Sigma dash (Sigma-) is a Type 3 letter

dual-dash.definition: A letter type (Type 5) where both hands dash simultaneously.
examples: Phi-, Psi-, Lambda-
Only 3 letters in this type

diamond.definition: A grid mode where hands are placed only on cardinal points (N, E, S, W). The default grid mode.
examples: Standard positions like alpha1 (N/S) use diamond mode

box.definition: A grid mode where hands are placed only on intercardinal points (NE, SE, SW, NW).
examples: Position beta5 (both hands at NE) uses box mode

skewed.definition: A grid mode introduced in Level 4 where one hand is on a cardinal point and one is on an intercardinal point.
examples: Hand at N and hand at NE
Creates zeta and eta positions

pictograph.definition: A visual representation of one beat of motion in TKA. Shows two props, arrows indicating motion, and position glyphs.
examples: Each letter has multiple pictograph variations
Pictographs can be sequenced to create choreography

variation.definition: A specific instance of a letter with particular starting/ending positions and locations. Each letter can have many variations.
examples: Letter A has variations starting from alpha1, alpha3, etc.
Variations differ by rotation direction and grid locations

cardinal.definition: The four main compass points on the grid: North (N), East (E), South (S), West (W).
examples: Diamond mode uses cardinal points
N is at the top of the pictograph

intercardinal.definition: The four diagonal compass points on the grid: Northeast (NE), Southeast (SE), Southwest (SW), Northwest (NW).
examples: Box mode uses intercardinal points
NE is at the top-right of the pictograph

cw.definition: Clockwise rotation direction, as viewed from above the performer.
examples: Hand path moving N -> E -> S -> W is clockwise

ccw.definition: Counter-clockwise rotation direction, as viewed from above the performer.
examples: Hand path moving N -> W -> S -> E is counter-clockwise

vtg.definition: Vertical Timing Glyph - a notation showing the relative timing of the two hands during a beat.
examples: Shows whether hands move together, split, or in sequence

reversal.definition: A change in prop rotation direction during a movement. Shown as dots on the pictograph.
examples: Prop changes from clockwise to counter-clockwise mid-beat

turns.definition: The number of full prop rotations during a beat. Common values are 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2.
examples: 0 turns = prop doesn't rotate
1 turn = full 360 degree rotation
